I know this probably sounds dumb, but it doesn’t feel dumb at 2am when I’m standing there re-wiping the counter because my glove brushed it. I keep thinking, if I skip a step, they’ll get sick and it’s on me.

Can you give me something practical here—like an SOP? Not therapy talk. Just a simple routine that’s “good enough” for a guy who’s dragging. And how do I time-box this stuff so I’m not losing an hour every night doing the same damn checks?

First, streamline your entry process: Boots off, clothes in a bag, straight to laundry. Wipe down phone and keys with a disinfectant wipe right there—takes 30 seconds. Hit the doorknobs once as you move through. That’s your core “decon” step, done in under 5 minutes.

For timing, set a hard limit—say, 10 minutes total for cleaning when you get home. Use a timer on your phone. When it dings, you’re done, no second-guessing. If a worry pops up at 2am, tell yourself, “I followed the SOP. It’s enough.” Write that core routine on a sticky note by the door if you need a visual reminder.

This keeps it manageable while still protecting your family. You’re not skipping steps; you’re just making them efficient. If the worry still nags, take a slow breath and focus on resting your back. You’ve earned it. How does this sound for a start?

Just tell me plain. Is that routine actually good enough to keep them from getting sick from what I drag home off the warehouse? Because if you can’t say that, then what am I supposed to do—roll the dice on my own kids?

You’re not rolling the dice; you’re taking real, consistent steps to protect your kids.

If your sleeve grazes the counter, skipping a re-wipe isn’t likely to be the difference. Germs don’t jump that easily with a quick brush. Stick to the timer and trust the process.

For “once” on wipes: Use one fresh disinfectant wipe per item. One for phone, one for keys, one for doorknobs (all knobs in one go if they’re close). That’s it. No extras unless something’s visibly dirty.
